As we've seen from Reddit and are seeing with Voat, spamming and reputation (and valuing comments) are all concerns. I've spent a bunch of time in the cryptocurrency etc. world and I think it's worth taking some lessons from there. For instance, what would Voat think about using a Trust-Davis like system? I think, if implemented right, it could help prevent people from creating a million spam accounts to bypass site protection mechanisms.

Glance through this paper to see what Trust-Davis is.

Perhaps we could make CCP spendable for this?

Edit 1: I will add some summary points and expand more on what this is shortly so it's clearer.

Edit 2: So, Trust-Davis is an online reputation system that provides insurance against fraud by leveraging existing relationships between people. When you are first starting out in a system (selling, or in the context of Voat, as a community member), you are new and people don't know if they can trust you. The idea is that an existing user with more reputation could spend some of their hard-earned CCP (from making contributions the community finds valuable) to vouch that a new user is an upstanding person (has to be defined in context of Voat of course). So basically, you become tangibly liable for the reference you provide to this person. Let's say a person needs a CCP "vouch pot" of at least X to contribute on a given voat sub (perhaps each sub could have a different minimum, different rules on who vouches, etc.).

In some systems, a new person could pay an existing user money to get them to vouch for them if the existing user doesn't personally know them as well. So, someone could pay you to get their "insurance", but you still have to put your CCP on the line.

Then, lets say in a given sub, there is a clear contract that you must agree to for interaction rules or something. Let's say you enter into an agreement with a mod to do X or not do X. You have to be insured to join the sub. Then, if that person negs on the agreement, they are thrown out and the CCP that the other users put on the line to vouch for this person are gone, so it hurts their reputation too. If their rep goes too low perhaps it has negative consequences for them too.

In this system then, you couldn't just create a new random name and jump in and spam because you wouldn't be able to without someone vouching for you (or you'd have to spend some kind of "money" to get insurance, so there is a cost with each new identity). You could charge more if the person seems like they are higher risk.

I hope I did a decent job of explaining it. How exactly it would be applied to Voat would need to be thought about, but I think having some kind of system in place would be quite helpful, especially if Voat goes the whole crypto revenue-sharing route.

There's a lot more to it and if you're interested I recommend you read more into the paper!

Setting up your own server can be pretty simple solution especially given that you already have had been doing a private server with your son. I don't have the information or experience to suggest hardware or an internet speed at which will be suitable to your needs but I will go over the process of setting up a private for Minecraft/teamspeak so I apologize if I go over stuff you may already know.

First of all, your server should be able to handle the Minecraft and teamspeak both simultaneously. So the first step is getting the server clients, You may have/want to change some of the server properties. Other than that, you just need to set up port forwarding on your server and router which is not much of a hassle. With port forwarding your router, you just need to create a port forward for your teamspeak and Minecraft (which is usually in the advanced settings of your router). Both programs will have their own port that needs to be forwarded. So make sure that the correct port is being forwarded and the router points to the internal IP of your server.

You will also need to open up exceptions in the firewall of your server to let programs in/out of specific ports. This process is a lot like the process of the router but simpler. You pretty much just need to make outbound/inbound rules for Minecraft and teamspeak ports.

If you choose to set up your own private server and have any sort of quests, feel free to PM me or look up some youtube videos. Enjoy your new server with your son and his friends!
